messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty fired PD-GD-321 -> inference-queue-surge (us-west-2). Queue depth > 90% threshold, autoscaler not increasing replicas. Paging eng-oncall.

pagerduty-bot: PD-GD-321 has been delivered to rotation. Escalation policy: 5m -> 15m -> eng-sre.

javier: acked. I'm oncall, looking now. Any immediate customer reports?

mike: seeing p90 latency up, and 429s. quick metrics snapshot: queue_depth=27,400, in_flight=4,800, p95_latency=6.1s, 429_rate=3.4%. Region: us-west-2 only so far.

anya: checking autoscaler logs and cloud events. initial read: CAPI requests to provider failing with InsufficientInstanceCapacity + QuotaExceeded errors.

mike: pasted HPA status: ```
NAME                  REFERENCE               TARGETS   MINPODS  MAXPODS  REPLICAS
inference-workers     Deployment/inference    60%/80%   10       100      10
```
The HPA wants to scale but nodes aren't available. Cloud error in controller-manager: `InsufficientInstanceCapacity: Request failed` and provider API 403 on quota check.

javier: ok plan: 1) manual bump minReplicas to 50 to force pod creation (may still pending if no nodes). 2) enable fallback routing to small-model variant for non-critical traffic. 3) notify CS for customer impact. Who can open cloud quota request?

anya: opening account quota request now and a support ticket with cloud: ticket #CLD-11277. Also spinning up a manual node group as backup (on-demand) but need ops approval for spending.

ops-lead: approved emergency on-demand node group up to 40 instances. Please tag with incident:GD-321 and keep costs auditable.

mike: applying HPA patch now: ```
kubectl patch hpa inference-workers -n prod --type merge -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":50}}'
```
Note: many pods will enter Pending.

mike: k8s events: `0/0 nodes available: Insufficient cpu, failed to schedule`. Cloud shows instances provisioning but stuck in pending due to `LaunchTemplateQuotaExceeded`.

anya: opened quota increase with cloud support for LaunchTemplate/OnDemand. Support ETA ~ 18 minutes. Meanwhile manual on-demand nodegroup create started: ngr-create --zone us-west-2a --size 40 --type g5.2xlarge.

caroline: I'll draft a short customer-facing banner: "We're experiencing degraded generation latency and intermittent failures in us-west-2. Engineers are actively mitigating; some requests may fall back to smaller models. We'll update shortly." Posting to status page and pinging account reps.

javier: enable routing change for non-authoritative traffic to small-model: ```
# feature-flag toggle
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' https://console.internal/api/toggle -d '{"route":"/generate","fallback_model":"small-v2","percent":30}'
```
This should shave load by ~25%.

mike: nodes from manual group are starting, but kubelet bootstrap failing on some due to IAM role propagation. I'm running a cluster-join health check: ```
kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep Pending || true
# checking cloud-instance status
```

pagerduty-bot: PD-GD-321 -> acknowledged by javier. Next escalation disabled while ack present.

anya: cloud support responded: raised internal limit to allow template launch; instances now entering Running. ETA ~6m for all to join.

mike: seeing workers join, replicas increasing to 45, queue depth dropping to 9,200. p95 latency down to 2.8s. 429 rate falling. Rolling restart of batch-processor to reduce backlog pressure. Command: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/batch-processor -n prod`.

javier: good. Keep fallback routing at 20% for another 30m and then ramp down if stable. Caroline, notify CS and Customer Success channel that we turned on graceful fallback and manual capacity.

caroline: tweeted status update + emailed top 5 accounts. CS confirmed two accounts reported degraded throughput; no data loss reported.

mike: final checks: all desired replicas 52, ready 50, queue depth 2,100, p95 1.2s, 429 rate 0.1%. No new errors in autoscaler logs besides delayed scale decisions earlier.

javier: marking as mitigated. Will keep PD open for 1h monitoring then resolve. Summary for post-incident: autoscaler did not handle spot/quotas exhaustion; add autoscaler policy to detect provider quota failures and fallback to reserved on-demand pool; improve runbook to pre-warm on-demand NG when queue depth spike > X for Y mins.

ops-lead: please file follow-up tasks: cloud quota automation, reserve emergency nodegroup, update runbook.

incident-bot: PD-GD-321 -> mitigated by 4791234699. Monitoring window started.

javier: thanks everyone. I'll draft a short incident note and link to follow-ups in #postmortems. :thumbsup:
